KHDK Electronics browse by type pitch/octave octaver octave fuzz octave fuzz (1 octave up) browse by enclosure pedal KHDK Electronics Unicorn Blood - Octave Fuzz Published on January 20, 2019 KHDK Electronics octave fuzz (1 octave up) pedal Information KHDK Electronics "Buckle up Earthlings, welcome to immortality!" -  Controlled Sonic Mayhem in a Candy-Colored Box of Magic Technology Unicorn Blood is an octave fuzz pedal like no other: trippy, hyper-versatile, a true miracle worker. It's retro at heart, taking an iconic sound of an unforgettable era and beaming it straight into 2018 with modern features like True Bypass, Octatone and additional EQ controls. Step aboard a rainbow-colored sonic ride, expand your creative horizon and harness the rush reserved for those who partake of Unicorn Blood. Each pedal ships with a fragrant bag of Dark Matter's iconic espresso blend, the Unicorn Blood coffee. Vintage-voiced yet modern, Unicorn Blood fuzz brings the best tones of the 60s and 70s into the modern day. It entraps a classic retro fuzz, elevating it with tweakable features to create your own tonal blend. Massive Sound Range and Versatility Unicorn Blood thinks of you as a player in various situations. The 3 switches - Fat, Boost and Sludge - give you a massive sound range and versatility.  In combination with the Fat switch, the Sludge will give you a low-mid growl to always keep you on top of the mix. Combined with the Boost and Fat, you can get yourself right where you want to be frequency-wise. Stack it or Run it Dry It can hold its own on a dry pedalboard: flip on the Sludge to sound massive. The Fat boosts your mids and, together with the Boost, it will deliver a sound you'd normally need at least 3 other pedals to achieve. The pedal stacks just as beautifully. Turn the boost off and add an overdrive or a booster to turn the Unicorn Blood into a miracle worker. That's when it truly reaches its spazzy, vicious potential that will blow your mind. Intuitive and Highly Playable With any Setup Independent of your setup, the Unicorn Blood will make your sound outstanding. The switches are right where they belong, making it a highly intuitive pedal. Feeling lost? Flip a switch and it will get you right back. Feel it spin on its own? Stack it and it becomes huge. sources.excerpt: KHDK Electronics Unicorn Blood II Octave Fuzz - Pedal of the Day Reviews Demos Buy a Pedalboard Interviews Contact Navigation Menu Menu KHDK Electronics Unicorn Blood II Octave Fuzz Posted By Pedal of the Day on Monday, June 7, 2021 in Fuzz, KHDK Electronics, Octave | 0 comments --> --> We were first introduced to KHDK Electronics , the brainchild of Metallica’s Kirk Hammett and industry pro David Karon, when they first started releasing pedals in 2016. The Ghoul Screamer is their take on the classic Tube Screamer , on steroids, and we really dug it. So we were pretty excited to dive into the Unicorn Blood II Octave Fuzz, a mammoth of a dirt pedal not for the tame or timid – this thing crushes eardrums and melts faces with authority. The first version of the Unicorn Blood in 2018 became an instant collector’s item, limited to just 100 pieces worldwide. Thus, the need for this second iteration was born, and KHDK has delivered. Vintage-voiced yet modern, this octave fuzz brings the best tones of the 60s and 70s into the modern day. It entraps a classic retro fuzz, elevating it with tweakable features to create your own tonal blend. Volume and Fuzz are the two most straightforward controls on the Unicorn Blood II, with Treble and Bass coming in a close second. Once you activate the Octave footswitch, the Octatone control acts like the tone knob on your guitar, sounding excellent with a neck pickup and low tone setting. The Fat switch shifts the EQ curve of the Treble and Bass controls, producing either fatter or more scooped mids. The Boost switch offers a gain boost, while Sludge adds loads of massive bottom end into the pre-distortion section. The Unicorn Blood II Octave Fuzz uses discrete transistors and germanium diodes for an authentic, vintage fuzz tone. From straightforward rock to doom-y, stoner metal to all-out walls of octave-laden fuzz, the versatility shines through on this one. The wide range of each parameter allows you to really dial in the sound you’re after, or be able to wildly experiment to create sounds you’ve never heard before. Hell, if it’s good enough for Brent Hinds of Mastodon and Matt Pike from High On Fire , it’s good enough for us all! Cheers to Kirk, David and KHDK Electronics on a wonderfully diverse and sonically celebrated machine, one that’s sure to blow out speakers for years to come. Be sure to check out our demo below to get the scoop on this beast, and to hear it in action!
